interface.title: सखा (Sakha) - The Sanskrit Parser
interface.stage_of_work: close reading and analysis of primary texts
interface.what_it_is_for: You paste a Sanskrit sentence in any common script and get back a word segmentation that resolves sandhi and compounds, morphological tags for each word, dictionary and dhatu links, a syllable and phoneme breakdown, and the analysis rendered in a script you choose.

data.note: There are no files and no demo button. I typed the sentences myself: a Bhagavad Gita line in Devanagari (धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः), an IAST verse full of compounds (rāmo rājamaṇiḥ sadā vijayate rāmaṃ rameśaṃ bhaje), a Harvard-Kyoto sentence (gacchati rAjaputro vanam) and the placeholder example वाग्देव्यै नमः. Both models called their remote servers and returned results.

features.name: Segment-and-tag table
features.general: Paste a sentence, run it, and read a one-line split of the sentence into words (sound changes undone, compounds split) above a numbered table with one row per word: surface form, base form and grammatical tags.
features.specific: Paste the Sanskrit and press Analyze with Model Dharmamitra. Read the Padaccheda line and the Word Analysis table (#, Word, Lemma, Grammar).
steps: Paste Sanskrit text into the text area
Press Analyze
Read the Padaccheda line
Read each row of Word Analysis
serves_tasks: Split running text into its words, undoing sound changes at word joins and splitting compound words into their members
Read the grammatical tags for each word

features.name: Analysis engine switch for comparison
features.general: Pick one of several analysis engines and run the same sentence through each to compare how they split it. Engines can differ in output: one may give only the word split, with no tag table.
features.specific: Switch Model between Dharmamitra and Hellwig (Segmentation Only); the change clears the results, so press Analyze again. Hellwig returns only the padaccheda (e.g. keeps राजमणिः whole where Dharmamitra gives राज + मणिः).
steps: Choose Model in the sidebar
Press Analyze and note the padaccheda
Switch Model and press Analyze again
Compare the two splits
serves_tasks: Compare two automatic methods on the same sentence

features.name: Configurable dictionary linking from word table
features.general: Choose which external reference a word's base form links to. The table then turns each base form into a lookup link, and verb forms into links to a separate root index.
features.specific: Pick Dictionary (Kosha.app, Ambuda or Sanskrit Kosha) and analyze again. Lemma cells become links to that dictionary, searched in Devanagari. Verb and participle forms in the Word column link to the ashtadhyayi.com dhatu search.
steps: Open the Dictionary dropdown
Choose Kosha.app, Ambuda or Sanskrit Kosha
Press Analyze again (any setting change clears the results)
Follow a lemma link, or a verb form's dhatu link; both lead outside the app
serves_tasks: Choose which reference dictionary the word links open
Go from an inflected verb form to its entry in a root index

features.name: Input/output script transliteration of results
features.general: Say which writing system the input is in (or let it be detected) and which one to show results in. The whole analysis, labels included, is then shown in the chosen script.
features.specific: Input Script is Auto-Detect or one of IAST, ISO, Harvard-Kyoto, SLP1, ITRANS, Velthuis, WX, Devanagari. Output Script also offers Indic scripts such as Grantha, Tamil, Telugu, Brahmi and Kannada. The padaccheda, words, lemmas and grammar labels are all transliterated.
steps: Type the text in any supported script
Leave Input Script on Auto-Detect or pick one
Choose an Output Script
Press Analyze and read the transliterated padaccheda and table
serves_tasks: Enter a sentence in whatever writing system it is in
Render the analysis in a different script or romanization

features.name: Syllable and phoneme breakdown panel
features.general: Open a collapsible panel that splits the input into syllables and individual sounds and shows counts of vowels, consonants and characters as headline numbers.
features.specific: Expand 'Varna & Akshara Analysis (Powered by Akshara)' to see Syllables, Spelling Breakdown and metrics for Svaras, Vyanjanas, Total Varnas and Total Characters, always in Devanagari.
steps: Analyze a sentence
Click the Varna & Akshara Analysis expander
Read the syllable list and the varna breakdown
Read the four count metrics
serves_tasks: Break the text into syllables and individual sounds, with counts

features.name: Bilingual interface toggle
features.general: Switch every label in the interface between English and the language being studied, and run the same workflow in either.
features.specific: The Language / भाषा radio switches between English and संस्कृतम्. Headings, column names, buttons and row numerals change. The input and settings are reset.
steps: Click संस्कृतम् (or English)
Re-enter the text
Press विश्लेषणं कुरु
Read पदच्छेदः and the पदविश्लेषणम् table
